identification: Six worn British silver half crowns: five Queen Victoria young head (shield reverse, 1839-1887 type, S.3889 range) and one George IV or William IV. Dates mostly illegible, Fair to Good, some corrosion spotting. Sterling (.925) so about 14.1 g each, roughly 85 g silver in total. Value is mainly bullion plus a small premium; no key date can be confirmed from the photos.

chrome_hint: eBay AU sold listings (Sold items filter): 'lot british silver half crowns victoria worn'; 'victoria young head half crown 1874 1883 1887 circulated'; 'george IV half crown 1820 1823 1825 worn'; 'william IV half crown 1834 1836 1837'. Terapeak for the same. Noble Numismatics (noble.com.au) past results: 'half crowns worn lot'. Leski and Downies results: 'half crowns silver .925 lot'. Also check current silver spot in AUD per troy ounce: six coins at about 14.1 g sterling is about 78.6 g fine silver, roughly 2.5 troy oz, for the melt floor.
viewing_check: Turn each coin over and read the date and reverse legend; any George IV (1820-1829) or William IV (1834-1837) coin, and any young head date like 1839, 1848, 1850s or 1880s with a key date (e.g. 1862-1863, 1881) would lift value. Check for cleaning, rim damage, and whether the odd-looking coin (centre right) is a genuine half crown or a counterfeit or token. Weigh the lot if possible (about 14 g per coin is genuine sterling).
